2026-11-18.title: Jindo County seeks in-home bathing providers
2026-11-18.summary: Jindo County reopened recruitment on November 17 for organizations to provide in-home bathing through its integrated community care program. Applicants must submit their materials in person to the county’s Integrated Care Team by November 23 at 6 p.m. local time.
2026-11-18.takeaway: Home-care equipment suppliers can use county notices like this to learn how Korea organizes local care delivery and which types of providers may be potential partners.

2026-11-18.title: Yeouido St. Mary’s and Soongsil expand clinical AI collaboration
2026-11-18.summary: Yeouido St. Mary’s Hospital said on November 17 that it signed a research cooperation agreement with Soongsil University’s AI-Bio Convergence Institute at a joint symposium on November 13. The symposium featured clinical research using large healthcare datasets and discussed future applications of AI in clinical medicine.
2026-11-18.takeaway: International clinical AI developers evaluating Korean validation partners can look to this hospital–university collaboration, although the announcement did not invite external applicants.

2026-11-18.title: Korea’s device regulator explains its innovative-device pathway
2026-11-18.summary: South Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety announced a November 16 forum on how innovative medical devices are designated and reviewed, including examples involving digital medical devices. The agenda also covered health insurance and software cybersecurity; the announcement did not introduce a new approval or reimbursement rule.
2026-11-18.takeaway: International device makers can use the agenda to identify which questions to raise about designation, evidence requirements and reimbursement before planning a Korean launch.

sources.label: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety release (Korean)

2026-11-19.title: Anseong links home nurses with visiting doctors
2026-11-19.summary: South Korea’s health minister visited Anseong’s home nursing center on November 18 to review how it coordinates care with local clinics. The center, jointly operated by the city and the Korean Nurses Association since September, provides services such as wound care and medication management for older adults with limited mobility.
2026-11-19.takeaway: Home-care suppliers evaluating Korean partners can use Anseong’s model to understand how municipal programs, nurses and clinics divide responsibility for care at home.

sources.label: Ministry of Health and Welfare release (Korean)

2026-11-19.title: Korean study tests an MRI marker after transient ischemic attack
2026-11-19.summary: In a study published on November 18, a Korean team compared 329 consecutive patients with transient ischemic attack and negative diffusion-weighted MRI according to whether a separate contrast-enhanced MRI marker was present. Recurrent ischemic stroke was more common in the marker-positive group (13.3% versus 3.0%), but the marker did not independently predict recurrence after adjustment.
2026-11-19.takeaway: Imaging companies planning Korean validation studies can use this design as a reference for testing whether a new marker adds predictive value beyond existing risk measures.

2026-11-19.title: Korea outlines hospital AI pilots and payment plans
2026-11-19.summary: At a November 18 government forum, Seoul National University Hospital and Premier Partners signed an agreement to identify clinical needs and support investment in medical AI for regional, essential and public care. The health ministry discussed linking field pilots to its public-hospital AI network and reviewing reimbursement approaches, but did not announce a new payment rate.
2026-11-19.takeaway: International medical AI vendors can follow the hospital pilot plans while budgeting separately for reimbursement, which remains under development.

sources.label: Ministry of Health and Welfare release (Korean)
